Instrument (EN): Cross-Cultural Oncology Measure for Perception and Awareness of Stigma Scale — US/Malawi original research
Scales / measured domains (EN): Anticipated cancer stigma (8); Internalized cancer stigma (8); Enacted cancer stigma (12); three proposed domains. CFA fit limited CFI .859 / RMSEA .112 / SRMR .063, not definitive cross-country equivalence.
Research provenance: Kimani et al., International Journal of Cancer 158 (2026), first online 2025-12-24, DOI 10.1002/ijc.70314. 209 adults receiving cancer care in Salt Lake City, Utah (USA) and Lilongwe (Malawi); initial 50 items, final 28. Reported alpha .92-.97. CFA indices CFI .859, RMSEA .112 mean psychometric limitation; no verified independent linguistic invariance.
DB locales: Production read-only 2026-10-28: 149 published unique keys/234 locale versions EN154 RU80 ES0; COMPASS-28 absent; distinguish preexisting hh-closeness-compass/meaning-compass.
EN form: Original English-language paper; original US study, but final English respondent form and its separate rights must be checked. No independently validated EN translation.
RU form: No validated Russian COMPASS respondent edition verified.
ES form: No validated Spanish COMPASS respondent edition verified.
Other translations: Malawi cohort and cross-cultural study are NOT evidence of independently validated Chichewa language adaptation, translated items, or cross-language measurement invariance. Respondent-language administration must be confirmed.
Target population: Adults with cancer recruited from two oncology clinics, Utah USA and Lilongwe Malawi, N=209; nonrepresentative convenience cohorts.
Commercial digital use / permission revi: Open-access CC BY article does not automatically clear third-party source item wording, questionnaire electronic reproduction, commercial SaaS scored administration, translation, or norm rights; review Data S1 source attributions and request scale-holder consent before activation.
Verification notes / safety gate: Research metadata only; first published 2025-12-24, NOT a new Oct2026 scale. CFA below typical strong fit (CFI .859, RMSEA .112); avoid claiming universal validity. Cancer-related sensitive disclosures; no patient clinical decisions, no item texts/scoring, no site release.

Instrument (EN): Cyberostracism Measure for Indian Young Adults — 42-item preliminary content/face-validity research pool
Scales / measured domains (EN): Direct digital exclusion experiences; subtle exclusion experiences; post-ostracism reactions. These are conceptual CONTENT AREAS, NOT established psychometric/scored factors. NO EFA/CFA and no validated cutoffs.
Research provenance: Sambath I, Kosalram KB. BMC Psychology 14 article 1545 (2026), first online 2026-07-29; version of record 2026-10-26, DOI 10.1186/s40359-026-05170-5. Initial 70→60 after 2 purposive groups n30 each; 8 content experts, 2 English language reviewers, face validity in 10 adolescents, final 42. S-CVI/Ave .88 and S-FVI/Ave .98, NO factorial validation.
DB locales: Live 2026-10-28 published Supabase app.assessment_versions: 149 keys, 234 published locales EN154 RU80 ES0; no CMIYA.
EN form: English expert linguistic-review evidence does not establish a independently psychometrically validated EN respondent questionnaire; original administered language must be confirmed.
RU form: No independently validated Russian-language respondent form.
ES form: No independently validated Spanish-language respondent form.
Other translations: Indian young-adult context; no independently confirmed separate language adaptation (e.g. Hindi/Tamil/Bengali), translation or equivalence study.
Target population: Indian young adults 18–24 in qualitative/cognitive interviewing (two groups of 30); expert reviewers and face-validity 10 adolescents; not a large representative factor-analytic cohort.
Commercial digital use / permission revi: BMC paper explicitly CC BY-NC-ND 4.0: does not grant commercial digital item redistribution or adaptation; written rights-holder permission and approved complete 42-item questionnaire, factor analysis, scoring and respondent consent required.
Verification notes / safety gate: PRELIMINARY research development ONLY. Article first online 2026-07-29 vs record version 2026-10-26. NO validated latent scales, total-score interpretation, cutoffs or diagnostic use. Context can involve adolescent participants; protect sensitive digital bullying/exclusion data.

Instrument (EN): Self-Efficacy in Addressing Menstrual Needs Scale — original Bangladesh schoolgirls 26-item edition
Scales / measured domains (EN): Menstrual Hygiene Preparation and Maintenance (17); Menstrual Pain Management (5); Executing Stigmatized Tasks (4). ORIGINAL journal 17+5+4=26; EMERGE online scoring item list only enumerates 16+5+4=25, needs exact reconciled item map before implementation.
Research provenance: Hunter EC et al., PLOS ONE 17(10):e0275736, published 2022-10-06, DOI 10.1371/journal.pone.0275736. 381 post-menarcheal Bangladeshi schoolgirls 9–17 from urban/rural schools, retest subsample n42. Original 34 survey items reduced by EFA to 26, alpha .86/.87/.77. EFA only, no independent CFA.
DB locales: 2026-10-28 live Supabase 149 published keys/234 locale records EN154 RU80 ES0; no SAMNS-26 key published.
EN form: English translated survey form available in article supplement; NOT independently psychometrically validated English-language respondent edition. Journal language English is not form validation.
RU form: No independently validated RU-RU translation verified.
ES form: No independently validated ES-ES translation verified.
Other translations: Original Bangla/Bengali Bangladesh respondent edition studied; English translation supplied in supporting material but NOT separate validated EN adaptation. No other independently validated translation verified.
Target population: 381 schoolgirls aged 9–17 after menarche in urban/rural Bangladesh; n42 two-week retest. School/minor population, not adult clinical screening.
Commercial digital use / permission revi: PLOS paper CC BY4 covers licensed article/supplements absent exceptions; author/source attribution is needed, but commercial hosted scored instrument use, original Bengali form and translation ownership, minors' consent/privacy and complete item mapping require dedicated clearance. Do not ingest participants' private data.
Verification notes / safety gate: RESEARCH ONLY. Study originally published 2022, not 2026. 17+5+4 is source journal final scale, while EMERGE site listed first-subscale 16 items (omits one item among 26); unresolved official scoring discrepancy prohibits digitization. EFA without independent CFA, requires replication and safeguarding for minors.
